Trellis · v0.2.0

Quickstart

Install the plugin, tell one repository about it, and do a first piece of work under contract. Ten minutes, four commands.

1 Install

There is no build and no installer — a plugin is distributed as source. The only prerequisite is Node on your PATH. 

claude plugin marketplace add yainierc/trellis
claude plugin install trellis@gmstek

Check it landed:

claude plugin details trellis@gmstek
  Hooks (4)  PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop

Keep the plugin path handy — the templates and the validator live inside it: 

TRELLIS=$(echo ~/.claude/plugins/cache/gmstek/trellis/*/)

2 Wire up a repository

Installing changes nothing on its own. A repository opts in by carrying a profile — the file that tells Trellis how to build, test and lint here. 

mkdir -p .trellis
cp $TRELLIS/templates/project-profile.yml .trellis/profile.yml

Open it and fill in the commands that actually exist in this repo:

commands:
  build:     dotnet build MySolution.sln
  test_fast: dotnet test --filter Category=Unit
  lint:      ~                      # `~` = none here; the gate is skipped and says so

git:
  base_branch:    main
  branch_pattern: "task/{id}-{slug}"
Read this once

A field set to ~ means "not applicable here". The gate that would have used it is skipped out loud, never silently. Leaving a real command out is not the same as declaring there isn't one.

3 Know when it is guarding you

Trellis is deliberately silent outside the situation it was built for. Two conditions arm it, and both must hold.

4 Do a piece of work

A spec answers what and why for a whole capability. A contract is one unit of work inside it. The branch is what turns the guardrails on.

The four commands

cp $TRELLIS/templates/SPEC.md      docs/specs/my-feature.md
cp $TRELLIS/templates/CONTRACT.md  docs/contracts/MY-T-01.md

node $TRELLIS/scripts/validate-contract.mjs docs/contracts --all

git checkout -b task/MY-T-01-short-slug

Now work. The hardest and most valuable part of the contract is done_when: it forces you to decide how "done" gets checked before any code exists. Prefer runnable commands — the gate re-executes them verbatim.

5 What it will stop you doing

Only while a contract is in flight. Each refusal explains itself and cites its rule.

AttemptResult
Edit a file outside writesDenied — scope is never widened mid-flight
Edit the contract you are executingDenied — a wrong contract is fixed by a human, in a separate commit
git push, gh pr create, git rebase, branch switchDenied — you commit in your worktree and stop there
Push to main or force-pushDenied always, contract or not
Finish with a red buildAllowed to stop — but the contract is marked blocked and you are told
Not a sandbox

These are defence in depth against drift, not a security boundary. A determined shell can evade a pattern, and that is by design — the goal is that nobody wanders out of scope by accident.

6 Staying current

claude plugin update trellis@gmstek
If you maintain the plugin

The install cache is keyed by version. New commits without a version bump in plugin.json reach nobody, and update will happily report already at the latest version. Bump it, then claude plugin tag --push.
